subject: chemistry

hotspots.label: Element samples
hotspots.description: Pure element samples: gold, carbon, oxygen, helium. Each is a substance made of exactly one kind of atom.
hotspots.positionHint: The four samples arranged in a row.
hotspots.function: Shows pure substances made of a single kind of atom.

hotspots.label: Identical atoms
hotspots.description: Zoom into the gold and every atom is a gold atom. One element = one kind of atom, repeated billions of times.
hotspots.positionHint: The atom cluster revealed when the zoom-in layer is on.
hotspots.function: Shows that an element is all identical atoms.

hotspots.label: Elements combining
hotspots.description: When elements bond, they form a new substance — a compound. Hydrogen and oxygen bond into water; the raw ingredients become something new.
hotspots.positionHint: The hydrogen and oxygen atoms merging into a water molecule, visible when the combine layer is on.
hotspots.function: Shows elements bonding into a compound.

visualStyleNotes: Chemistry palette, Anatomy Atelier bar: warm off-white/paper background (#F7F3EC) with a soft radial vignette, no floor grid, no props. Four floating element samples in a row, lit with soft neutral studio light — no rim-light glow, no bloom, no emissive anywhere. Clean stylized product-render look, specimen-quality not cartoon. Gold: soft warm-yellow chunk; carbon: soft graphite block; oxygen: translucent pale-blue puff; helium: translucent pale-gray puff. Strong saturated color is reserved for the small flat hotspot dots (amber / coral / molecular-green accents from the Chemistry palette). Slow auto-rotation, calm, minimal chrome.
materialNotes: Metallic-roughness PBR, metallic=0 everywhere except gold (metallic ~0.7) and carbon (roughness ~0.8), single 2K shared texture atlas. Gold chunk: warm yellow, metallic 0.7. Carbon block: soft graphite, roughness 0.8. Oxygen/helium puffs: translucent pale, alpha ~0.3. No emissive channels anywhere — any glow is handled by app runtime UI.
assetBrief:
SUBJECT: samples of pure elements, built to be read as 'pure substances — one kind of atom each — that combine to make everything.' Three procedural layers, all clean primitives:

1) MAIN: four element samples in a row (spacing ~1.2): (a) a small gold chunk — a few rounded soft warm-yellow polyhedra; (b) a carbon block — a soft graphite cube; (c) an oxygen puff — a soft translucent pale-blue rounded cloud; (d) a helium puff — a soft translucent pale-gray rounded cloud.

2) ZOOM INTO ATOMS (toggleable layer): the camera eases into the gold chunk (app-driven) and it dissolves into a cluster of identical warm-yellow atom spheres (radius ~0.18) — all the same kind, all gold.

3) COMBINE INTO COMPOUND (toggleable layer): a hydrogen atom (small warm off-white sphere) and an oxygen atom (small muted red sphere) float up from the samples and bond into a water molecule (104.5° ball-stick with a thin graphite rod) — a compound made from two elements.

Camera: framed so all four samples fit with negative space; auto-rotate default. Budget 8-12k triangles. Named nodes: GoldChunk, CarbonBlock, OxygenPuff, HeliumPuff, GoldAtomCluster, GoldAtoms, HydrogenAtom, OxygenAtom, WaterMolecule, WaterBond. All labels are hotspot dots in the app layer.
